answer: Each PoA identity must complete a challenge-bound chain of modular squarings, with each result feeding the next; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the endpoint efficiently. GPUs can run separate clones concurrently, but cannot shortcut one chain by splitting its dependent steps, so each added identity requires another full interval of sequential computation. This creates a physical time and hardware cost for Sybil identities; lotus, trellis, and dune denote distinct challenges, not parallel paths.
